correctness.rationale: For compactly supported measures the negative-binomial Schur bound yields a bounded operator, and reflection yields self-adjointness. The elementary compact-support Laplace principle gives each diagonal logarithmic rate log(4s(1-s)), while binomial large deviations centered at support point s give offdiagonal rate zero. Subtraction proves the exact positive normalized logarithmic growth and hence eventually strictly negative 2-by-2 minors. The two-atom prefactor follows from local binomial Stirling estimates. At delta_(1/2), an explicit Gamma-integral Gram representation gives positivity. Rational exact tests check examples but the proof covers every measure in scope.

originality.rationale: The claim is a necessary midpoint-support condition for positive-semidefinite generalized Hilbert matrices, strengthened to the universal exact exponential rate of a negative 2-by-2 principal compression. This is not a norm bound or a statement that entries are positive. Read primary results in the three relevant works give boundedness/adjoint/Hankel or weighted-norm theorems, not this support obstruction. published-finding corpus semantic queries on the exact kernel, reflection symmetry, PSD, two-point measures and midpoint yielded no equivalent or stronger implication. Remaining priority risk: a differently named matrix positivity criterion in specialized literature or uninspected portions of an adjacent operator paper.
residual_risks: An equivalent PSD criterion could be recorded under an alternate negative-binomial matrix name.

value.rationale: For the established Hausdorff-induced generalized Hilbert matrix family, distinguishing entrywise positivity from operator positivity is a meaningful structural issue. The result gives an all-measure necessary support condition, sharp as a support-distance boundary, and a universal exponential strength of the 2-by-2 violation determined solely by the closest support point to 1/2. It applies equally to continuous, singular, and atomic measures and is not a routine norm computation or a one-parameter numerical observation.
